questions.q: Two bodies with kinetic energies in the ratio of 3:1 are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their masses is
questions.explanation: KE = p²/2m; for equal p, KE ∝ 1/m, so $KE_1/KE_2=m_2/m_1=3/1$, giving $m_1:m_2=1:3$.

questions.q: A horizontal force of 5 N is applied on a stationary body of mass 5 kg, which is initially at rest on a frictionless table. The change in kinetic energy of the body in 10 s is
questions.explanation: a = F/m = 1 m/s²; v = at = 10 m/s after 10s; ΔKE = ½mv² − 0 = ½×5×100 = 250 J.

questions.q: A body of mass 0.25 kg travels along a straight line from x = 0 to x = 2 m with a speed v = k x$^{3/2}$ where k = 2 SI units. The work done by the net force during this displacement is

During an elastic collision between two bodies, which of the following statements are correct? I. The initial kinetic energy is equal to the final kinetic energy of the system. II. The linear momentum is conserved. III. The kinetic energy during Δt (the collision time) is not conserved.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision total KE and momentum are conserved before and after (I, II true); during the brief collision time energy is momentarily stored as deformation energy so KE is not conserved instant-to-instant (III true). All three are correct.

questions.q: A particle of mass 500 g is at rest. It is free to move along a straight line. The power delivered to the particle varies with time according to the following graph [P increases linearly from 2 W at t=0 to 8 W at t=5s]. The momentum of the particle at t=5s is
questions.explanation: Work done = area under the P-t graph $=\dfrac{2+8}{2}\times5=25\,J=\dfrac{p^2}{2m}$; with $m=0.5$kg, $p=5\,kg\,m/s$.

questions.q: A ball of mass 0.2 kg is thrown vertically down from a height of 10 m. It collides with the floor and loses 50% of its energy and then rises back to the same height. The value of its initial velocity is
questions.explanation: To rise back to 10 m the rebound speed must be $\sqrt{2gh}$ = 14.14 ms$^{-1}$, so KE just after collision = 100m. This is half the KE just before collision, so KE before = 200m, giving speed before impact v = 20 ms$^{-1}$. Using v$^2$ = u$^2$+2gh: 400 = u$^2$+200, so u ≈ 14 ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A smooth chain of length 2 m is kept on a table such that its length of 60 cm hangs freely from the edge of the table. The total mass of the chain is 4 kg. The work done in pulling the entire chain on to the table is, (Take g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.explanation: Mass per unit length $=4/2=2$ kg/m; hanging mass $=2\times0.6=1.2$ kg with its centre of mass 0.3 m below the table. Work done $=1.2\times10\times0.3=3.6$ J.

questions.q: A 1 kg ball moving at 12 ms$^{-1}$ collides with a 2 kg ball moving in opposite direction at 24 ms$^{-1}$. If the coefficient of restitution is $\dfrac{2}{3}$, then their velocities after the collision are
questions.explanation: Using momentum conservation $v_1+2v_2=-36$ and restitution $v_2-v_1=e(u_1-u_2)=\tfrac23(36)=24$, solving gives $v_1=-28$ ms$^{-1}$ (1 kg ball) and $v_2=-4$ ms$^{-1}$ (2 kg ball).

questions.q: A ball hits the floor and rebounds after an inelastic collision. In this case
options: the momentum of the ball is conserved
the mechanical energy of the ball is conserved
the total momentum of the ball and the earth is conserved
the total mechanical energy of the ball and the earth is conserved
questions.explanation: The ball alone loses momentum and energy on rebound (inelastic), but treating the ball+earth as an isolated system, total momentum of the ball and earth together is conserved.

questions.q: A body is initially at rest. It undergoes one-dimensional motion with constant acceleration. The power delivered to it at time 't' is proportional to
questions.explanation: $v=at$ and $P=Fv=(ma)(at)=ma^2t$, so $P\propto t$.

questions.q: During inelastic collision between two objects, which of the following quantity always remains conserved ?
questions.explanation: In any collision, in the absence of external forces, total linear momentum of the system is always conserved, even though kinetic energy is not conserved in an inelastic collision.

questions.q: Two particles of masses m$_1$ and m$_2$ have equal kinetic energies. The ratio of their momenta is
questions.explanation: Since KE = p²/2m for equal KE, p ∝ $\sqrt{m}$, so p$_1$ : p$_2$ = $\sqrt{m_1}$ : $\sqrt{m_2}$.

questions.q: A motor pump lifts 6 tonnes of water from a well of depth 25 m to the first floor of height 35 m from the ground floor in 20 minutes. The power of the pump (in kW) is [g = 10 ms$^{-2}$]
questions.explanation: Total height raised = 25 + 35 = 60 m. $P = \dfrac{mgh}{t} = \dfrac{6000 \times 10 \times 60}{1200} = 3000$ W = 3 kW.

questions.q: A 12 kg bomb at rest explodes into two pieces of 4 kg and 8 kg. If the momentum of 4 kg piece is 20 Ns, the kinetic energy of the 8 kg piece is
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum the 8 kg piece also has momentum of magnitude 20 Ns (opposite direction). $KE = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{20^2}{2\times8} = 25$ J.

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 4 kg and momentum 6 Ns will be
questions.explanation: KE $=\dfrac{p^2}{2m}=\dfrac{6^2}{2\times4}=\dfrac{36}{8}=4.5$ J.

questions.q: A truck accelerates from speed v to 2v. Work done in during this is
options: three times as the work done in accelerating it from rest to v.
same as the work done in accelerating it from rest to v.
four times as the work done in accelerating it from rest to v.
less than the work done in accelerating it from rest to v.
questions.explanation: Work done = $\Delta KE$. From $v$ to $2v$: $\dfrac12 m(4v^2-v^2)=\dfrac32 mv^2$, which is 3 times the work $\dfrac12 mv^2$ done in accelerating from rest to $v$.

questions.q: A body of mass 'm' is travelling with a velocity 'u'. When a constant retarding force 'F' is applied, it comes to rest after travelling a distance 's$_1$'. If the initial velocity is '2u', with the same force 'F', the distance travelled before it comes to rest is 's$_2$'. Then,
questions.explanation: By the work-energy theorem $Fs=\frac12mv^2$, so $s\propto v^2$; doubling the initial speed quadruples the stopping distance, giving s$_2$ = 4s$_1$.

questions.q: Two bodies of masses m$_1$ and m$_2$ are acted upon by a constant force F for a time t. They start from rest and acquire kinetic energies E$_1$ and E$_2$ respectively. Then $\dfrac{E_1}{E_2}$ is
questions.explanation: Both bodies gain the same momentum p=Ft; since $E=p^2/2m$, $E_1/E_2=m_2/m_1$.

questions.q: A body of mass 5 kg is thrown vertically up with a kinetic energy of 490 J. The height at which the kinetic energy of the body becomes half of the original value is ................. (acceleration due to gravity = 9.8 $ms^{-2}$).
questions.explanation: Initial KE $=490$ J gives $v^2=196$; at half KE, $v'^2=98$. Using $v'^2=v^2-2gh$: $98=196-19.6h \Rightarrow h=5$ m.

questions.q: If the linear momentum of a body is increased by 50%, then the kinetic energy of that body increases by .......................
questions.explanation: $KE=p^2/2m$. With $p'=1.5p$, $KE'/KE=(1.5)^2=2.25$, i.e. an increase of 125%.

questions.q: Two rectangular blocks A and B of masses 2 kg and 3 kg respectively are connected by a spring of spring constant $10.8\ \text{Nm}^{-1}$ are placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The block 'A' was given an initial velocity of $0.15\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ [towards B]. The maximum compression of the spring during the motion is
questions.explanation: Maximum compression occurs at common velocity $v'=\dfrac{2\times0.15}{5}=0.06\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. Energy stored $=\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(0.15)^2-\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(0.06)^2=0.0225-0.009=0.0135\ \text{J}=\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2 \Rightarrow x=0.05\ \text{m}$.

questions.q: The work done by a force acting on a body is as shown in the graph [F(N) vs S(m): F rises linearly from 0 to 10 N as S goes 0 to 5 m, stays constant at 10 N from S=5 to 15 m, then rises linearly from 10 N to 20 N as S goes from 15 to 20 m]. The total work done in covering an initial distance of 20 m is
questions.explanation: Work = area under F-S graph = triangle (0-5m): $\tfrac{1}{2}\times5\times10=25$ J, rectangle (5-15m): $10\times10=100$ J, trapezium (15-20m): $\tfrac{1}{2}(10+20)\times5=75$ J; total $=25+100+75=200$ J.
